Stochastic Calculations

stochastic_calculations.Rmd
library(RFDose)

calculate_emf_doses_stochastic() gives the uncertainty of the doses. It calculates the doses of each row n times (default: 1000), each time with parameters, SAR values and input values drawn from their distributions (see Uncertainty in the stochastic model), and summarises the doses of all draws. It takes the same arguments as calculate_emf_doses(), including sar_file. Give a seed for reproducible results: the same seed and arguments give the same draws.

How to use stochastic calculations 

# Calculate example doses with their uncertainty
result <- calculate_emf_doses_stochastic(
  example_data, 
  tissue = "brain", 
  n = 1000, 
  seed = 1)
head(result)
#>   sample_id row      dose deterministic       mean         sd      q2.5
#> 1     TEST1   1 call_dose     73.158702  75.357657 44.1154544 22.257444
#> 2     TEST1   1 data_dose    203.099513 207.172960 79.6143357 99.613949
#> 3     TEST1   1 dect_dose     87.012757  84.171673 50.7442908 20.036082
#> 4     TEST1   1 farf_dose    160.649754 157.821709 65.5701609 45.433573
#> 5     TEST1   1 wifi_dose      2.804097   2.795889  0.7220588  1.710858
#> 6     TEST1   1 lptp_dose     11.419562  11.236501  4.1954528  5.009065
#>          q50      q97.5
#> 1  65.971687 186.105093
#> 2 192.077063 404.876663
#> 3  72.585983 208.906906
#> 4 151.360612 304.949104
#> 5   2.684747   4.469926
#> 6  10.532281  21.167345

The result has one row per row of data and exposure source, plus the total dose (total_dose), in mJ/kg/day:

 sample_id row       dose deterministic  mean    sd  q2.5   q50 q97.5
     TEST1   1  call_dose          73.2  75.4  44.1  22.3  66.0 186.1
     TEST1   1  data_dose         203.1 207.2  79.6  99.6 192.1 404.9
     ...
     TEST1   1 total_dose         565.0 565.9 119.0 367.6 551.3 828.0
Column Description
sample_id, row ID (if data has a column sample_id) and row number in data
dose Exposure source (as the columns of calculate_emf_doses()), or total_dose for their sum
deterministic Dose with the values of the parameter file, as calculated by calculate_emf_doses()
mean, sd Mean and standard deviation of the doses of all draws
q2.5, q50, q97.5 Median and 95% interval of the doses of all draws (other quantiles with probs)

Options:

  • sar_sd: standard deviation of the SAR values, relative to their value (default: 0.25). With 0, the SAR values are not drawn
  • draw_inputs = FALSE: the input values are not drawn, so the uncertainty comes from the parameters and SAR values only
  • distributions, input_distributions: own distribution files (YAML), with the structure of the inbuilt files params_distributions.yaml and input_distributions.yaml
  • keep_draws = TRUE: also returns the doses, parameters and inputs of every draw
  • seed: random seed for reproducible draws (as set.seed() before, but without changing the random state of the session)

The calculation takes about 25 seconds for the 3 rows of the example data with 1000 draws, and grows with the number of rows and draws.

# Uncertainty from the parameters and SAR values only, with the GOLIAT SAR values (average of the four phantoms)
calculate_emf_doses_stochastic(
  example_data, 
  tissue = "brain", 
  sar_file = "goliat_average", 
  draw_inputs = FALSE)

Uncertainty in the stochastic model

calculate_emf_doses_stochastic() draws three kinds of values. Each distribution is centred on the value used by the deterministic calculation, and only its shape is given in the distribution files:

Drawn values Distributions File
Parameters (260): output powers, duty cycles, proportions, far-field power densities Lognormal and truncated lognormal (powers), beta (duty cycles, single proportions), Dirichlet (proportions that sum to 1, drawn together); mean = value in params.yaml params_distributions.yaml
SAR values Lognormal around their value, with a relative standard deviation of 25% (sar_sd). SAR values from the same simulation are drawn together; SAR values of 0 stay 0 -
Inputs (27): durations, proportions, urbanicity, commuting time Truncated lognormal for durations (relative standard deviation 20%, between 0 and 86400 s), beta and Dirichlet for proportions, categorical for urbanicity (given value kept with probability 0.8); centred on the value in data, or on the default value if missing. Durations of 0 stay 0 input_distributions.yaml

Every row is calculated with the same parameter sets, and the inputs of a row are drawn around its own values, so the doses of a row do not depend on the other rows. The distribution files are generated from the same Excel file as the parameters and default values (data-raw/source_params/).
